Action Mode engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Action Mode rollout covers storefront language. Xcode, system frameworks, and Connect actually separate in-app video stabilization from product-page copy:

  • Camera Action Mode & system stabilization UI — Apple Camera feature that applies extra video stabilization for handheld walking and running footage on iPhone 14 and later. Controls in-device capture behavior — not App Store language.
  • AVFoundation & video capture pipelines — frameworks some apps use to record video with custom stabilization before or after export. Your listing may mention stabilized handheld video; building capture pipelines is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Core Motion & gyro-based stabilization — separate in-app surfaces where recorded footage may be smoothed with motion data. Listing copy explains those buyer benefits; stabilization algorithm engineering is outside AppLocale scope.
  • Camera permissions & capture entitlements — NSCameraUsageDescription, microphone access, and background audio when recording video. Entitlements and capture wiring are platform work — distinct from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains Action Mode to buyers.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Action Mode support in the binary.

A working Action Mode or handheld-stabilization story and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Action Mode vs Cinematic Mode vs Macro vs Photographic Styles vs Action Button vs Camera Control — do not conflate

US/EU indie teams often merge six Camera string families. This page covers product-page listing copy that markets Action Mode — extra video stabilization for handheld walking and running footage — not cinematic depth-of-field, not macro close-ups, not still-photo tone presets, not hardware side buttons, and not dedicated camera hardware controls:

  • Action Mode & handheld stabilization marketing (this page) — paragraphs and frame text explaining "Action Mode", "Stabilized video", "Handheld stabilization", "Smooth walking footage", "Smooth running footage", 动作模式, 运动防抖, and 手持稳定视频. Toggle Action Mode → record while walking or running → smoother handheld video.
  • Cinematic Mode listing copy (different) — shallow-depth cinematic video look with focus transitions: "Cinematic Mode", "Cinematic video", 浅景深电影效果视频, 电影效果模式. Depth-of-field storytelling — not extra stabilization for walking-running footage. Not this page.
  • Macro & Macro Control listing copy (different) — close-up macro photography at minimum focus distance: "Macro", "Macro Control", 微距, 微距近拍, 微距控制. Still-photo close-ups — not handheld video stabilization. Not this page.
  • Photographic Styles listing copy (different) — still-photo tone presets in Camera: Photographic Styles, Rich Contrast, Vibrant, Warm, Cool, 摄影风格, 静物色调预设, 丰富对比度, 鲜明, 暖色, 冷色. Photo color grading — not video stabilization. Covered on a separate Photographic Styles guide — not Action Mode copy.
  • Action Button listing copy (different) — the physical side button on iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 16 family devices configured under Settings → Action Button: 操作按钮, 灵动按钮. Hardware button assignment — not Camera Action Mode video stabilization. Covered on our Action Button guide.
  • Camera Control listing copy (different) — the dedicated camera control on iPhone 16: light press, half-press, slide, click for capture. 相机控制, 相机控制按钮. Hardware capture control — not Action Mode stabilization toggle marketing. Covered on our Camera Control guide.
  • Portrait mode & Night Mode (different) — portrait background blur and low-light still or video capture are separate Camera surfaces with different screenshot vocabulary — not Action Mode handheld stabilization.

Cinematic Mode adds cinematic depth-of-field to video. Action Mode adds stabilization to handheld walking-running video. Macro captures extreme close-ups. Photographic Styles adjust still-photo tone. Action Button assigns a hardware side button. Camera Control is a dedicated capture control. Mixing vocabulary across those surfaces on one product page reads like confused localization — scope each screenshot frame to the workflow it actually shows.

Action Mode-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Handheld stabilization listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's Action Mode feature — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Action Mode phrasing

US pages use "Action Mode", "Stabilized video", "Handheld stabilization", "Smooth walking footage", "Smooth running footage", or "Record while you move." Apple's Simplified Chinese Camera vocabulary often uses 动作模式 for the branded Action Mode toggle, 运动防抖 for motion-stabilization marketing, and 手持稳定视频 for handheld walking and running footage positioning. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing stabilization capabilities your app does not support.

Walking vs running vs general handheld

Screenshot overlays differ by use case — walking down a street, jogging, hiking with the phone in hand. Chinese buyers expect concise action labels on gallery frames: 边走边拍 for walk-and-record, 跑步拍摄 for running footage, 手持稳定 for general handheld stabilization. Mixing English "Action Mode" with Chinese body copy on the same frame looks inconsistent.

Action Mode vs generic video stabilization

When your English listing markets both Apple's Action Mode branding and generic "video stabilization" or "gyro stabilization" terms, zh-Hans overlays may use 动作模式 for Apple's branded toggle and 运动防抖 for generic stabilization search intent — distinct buyer promises with different screenshot vocabulary on the same product page.

Before-and-after shaky vs smooth footage

Many Action Mode marketing screenshots show side-by-side shaky vs stabilized walking or running clips. zh-Hans caption lines should name the workflow step the frame shows: 动作模式 for the toggle, 运动防抖 for stabilization outcome, 手持稳定视频 for the walking-running use case — not English "Before / After" pasted through machine translation.

Do not conflate with Cinematic Mode, Macro, or Action Button

Action Mode stabilizes handheld walking-running video. Cinematic Mode adds shallow-depth cinematic look — different buyer promise. Macro captures close-up stills — not video stabilization. Action Button assigns a hardware side button — not Camera Action Mode. Camera Control is a dedicated capture hardware control — not stabilization toggle marketing. If your app supports multiple Camera surfaces, scope each screenshot frame accurately.

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need stabilization search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 动作模式, 运动防抖, and 手持稳定视频 each signal different intent from Cinematic Mode 电影效果 keywords or Macro 微距 keywords.

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines — rewritten from your English Action Mode marketing originals.

Can AppLocale implement Action Mode or AVFoundation stabilization?

No. We deliver listing metadata copy only. Video capture engineering, gyro stabilization wiring, and walking-running sample footage design are outside AppLocale scope.

How is this different from Cinematic Mode, Macro, Photographic Styles, Action Button, or Camera Control?

Action Mode copy markets extra video stabilization for handheld walking and running footage — 动作模式, 运动防抖, 手持稳定视频. Cinematic Mode copy markets shallow-depth cinematic video — 浅景深电影效果视频. Camera Control copy markets dedicated capture hardware — 相机控制. Each surface has separate screenshot vocabulary.

Should zh-Hans copy use 动作模式, 运动防抖, or 手持稳定视频?

Each appears in Chinese storefront and search contexts.
